hook.situation: Suggesting an option, trying food or clothes before deciding, and asking for help without sounding blunt.
objectives: Use V아/어 보세요 and V아/어 볼까요? for trying an action: 입어 보세요, 먹어 볼까요?
Use V아/어 주세요 for polite requests: 추천해 주세요, 보여 주세요, 도와주세요.
Use Vㄹ/을까요? to suggest or ask what to do: 같이 갈까요?, 주문할까요?
hook.whyItMatters: Korean suggestions often soften the action before the decision. 한번 입어 보세요 feels lighter than 입으세요, and 추천해 주세요 is clearer and more polite than a blunt command.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어 보다 — try doing V (give it a go)
grammarNotes.func: Add -아/어 보다 to a verb to mean "try doing something" — do it once and see how it goes. It's the warm, everyday way to nudge someone: "go ahead and try it."

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㅏ or ㅗ
formTable.ex: 가다 → 가 보다 (try going), 오다 → 와 보다 (try coming)

formTable.when: Stem ends in any other vowel
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹어 보다 (try eating), 읽다 → 읽어 보다 (try reading)
하다 → 해 보다 (try doing), 공부하다 → 공부해 보다 (try studying)

examples.note: 한번 ("give it a try") goes hand in hand with -아/어 보다 to soften a suggestion.
Past 봤어요 asks about experience — "have you ever tried it?"

examples.en: I want to try making Korean food.
examples.note: -아/어 보다 slots right into -고 싶다 when you want to give something a try.
묻다 is a ㄷ-irregular: 묻- → 물어, then + 보세요.

keyPoint.label: V-아/어 보다 vs. plain V
keyPoint.body: 먹으세요 just says "eat it." 먹어 보세요 says "try it and see how it is" — it frames the action as something new to test out, which makes the suggestion feel friendlier and less pushy.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 읽어 보세요, the ㄺ of 읽- links forward, so it sounds like [일거 보세요] — the ㄱ carries into the next syllable.

drill.instruction: Turn each verb into a friendly suggestion with -아/어 보세요 ("try ___-ing").
drill.model: 입다 (to wear) → 입어 보세요. (Try it on.)

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Here 보다 is already the main verb ("to look"), so you don't tack the helper 보다 on top of it. Doubling it — 봐 보세요 — sounds odd. Just say 보세요, or 한번 보세요 for the "give it a look" feel. The helper 보다 attaches to OTHER verbs (먹어 보세요, 읽어 보세요), not to 보다 itself.

grammarNotes.title: V-아/어 주세요 — please do V (for me)
grammarNotes.func: Add -아/어 주세요 to a verb to politely ask someone to do something for you. It's the normal, warm way to make a request — softer than a bare command.

formTable.when: Stem ends in ㅏ or ㅗ
formTable.ex: 앉다 → 앉아 주세요 (please sit), 보다 → 봐 주세요 (please look)

formTable.when: Stem ends in any other vowel
formTable.ex: 열다 → 열어 주세요 (please open), 기다리다 → 기다려 주세요 (please wait)
하다 → 해 주세요 (please do), 말하다 → 말해 주세요 (please tell me)

examples.note: With 주다 itself you just say 주세요; 좀 ("a little") softens it.

examples.en: Please open the door for me.
examples.note: 열다 → 열어 + 주세요; 좀 makes it gentler.
하다 verb: 말하다 → 말해 주세요. A really useful one for learners.
기다리다 → 기다려 주세요; the waiting is for your sake, so 주다 fits.

keyPoint.label: V-(으)세요 vs. V-아/어 주세요
keyPoint.body: 앉으세요 is a polite instruction aimed at what the listener does ("please sit"). 앉아 주세요 adds 주다 ("do it for me"), so it lands as a favor you'd be grateful for — exactly the feel of most polite English requests.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 열어 주세요 links across the ㄹ → [여러 주세요]; the ㄹ of 열- slides into the next syllable.

drill.instruction: Make a polite request with -아/어 주세요 ("please ___ for me").

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English "please" can't tell apart a plain instruction from a favor. -(으)세요 on its own can sound like an order or a general direction; adding 주다 (기다려 주세요) marks the action as done for your benefit — which is what most polite English requests really mean.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㄹ까요? — shall we? / should I?
grammarNotes.func: Add -(으)ㄹ까요? to a verb to suggest doing something together ("shall we?") or to ask what the listener thinks about you doing it ("should I?"). It's the standard way to float a friendly idea.

formTable.ex: 가다 → 갈까요? (shall we go?), 마시다 → 마실까요? (shall we drink?)
먹다 → 먹을까요? (shall we eat?), 앉다 → 앉을까요? (shall we sit?)
놀다 → 놀까요? (shall we hang out?), 만들다 → 만들까요? (shall we make it?)

examples.note: 우리 같이 ("we, together") makes the group "shall we?" clear.

examples.en: Shall we watch a movie tomorrow?
examples.note: 보다 ends in a vowel → 볼까요?; a casual invite to do something together.
열다 ends in ㄹ, so just add -까요? → 열까요?. Here it asks the listener's opinion: "should I?"
만나다 → 만날까요?; question words like 어디 fit right in.

keyPoint.label: V-(으)ㄹ까요? vs. V-아/어요
keyPoint.body: 먹어요 states or mildly pushes ("(let's) eat"). 먹을까요? turns it into a real question that hands the decision to the listener — you propose, they answer. Reach for -(으)ㄹ까요? when you actually want their okay, not just to announce the plan.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: The 까 is always tense (ㄲ): 먹을까요? sounds like [머글까요]. The ㄱ of 먹- links forward into 을.

drill.instruction: Turn each verb into a "shall we?" suggestion with -(으)ㄹ까요?.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: After seeing 먹다 → 먹을까요?, learners often glue 을 onto ㄹ-stems too. But ㄹ-stems already end in a vowel-like ㄹ that carries the sound, so you just add -까요?: 놀다 → 놀까요?, 만들다 → 만들까요?, 열다 → 열까요?. No extra 을.

grammarNotes.title: V-(으)ㅂ시다 — formal "let's" for groups
grammarNotes.func: Use -(으)ㅂ시다 to suggest that a group do something in a formal or public setting. It sounds organized and official, so it fits meetings, announcements, campaigns, and speeches. For friends, use -자; for a softer suggestion, use -(으)ㄹ까요?

examples.note: A natural meeting-room use: formal, clear, and group-directed.

examples.en: Let's get off at the next station.
examples.note: Announcement-like and organized, not a casual friend-to-friend suggestion.
Works when someone leads a group at a dinner or event.
Campaign or public-message tone; 함께 makes the group invitation explicit.

keyPoint.label: -자 < -(으)ㄹ까요? < -(으)ㅂ시다
keyPoint.body: 가자 is casual and close. 갈까요? is softer because it asks the listener's opinion. 갑시다 is formal and group-leading — useful in meetings or public speech, but too stiff for close friends.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 시작합시다 and 건배합시다, the ㅂ before 시다 is held clearly, and 시다 is always pronounced tense, like [씨다] — 합시다 sounds like [합씨다] at any speed, though the spelling stays 합시다. Don't turn 합시다 into 하십니다 — that is a different ending.

drill.instruction: Change each verb into a formal group suggestion with -(으)ㅂ시다.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English "let's" can sound friendly upward, but -(으)ㅂ시다 can feel like you are leading or directing the other person. With a boss, teacher, or older person one-on-one, use a respectful question such as 가시겠어요? or 가실까요? instead.

exampleSentence.note: 하다 becomes 해 before 보다.
입다 becomes 입어 before 보다.
먹다 becomes 먹어 before 보다.

exampleSentence.en: Should we try going to this restaurant?
exampleSentence.note: 가다 becomes 가 before 보다.
추천해 주세요 is the useful request form.
Often softens a trial suggestion.
Useful when checking a choice after trying.

extendedVocabulary.english: how is it?; what do you think?

exampleSentence.note: 어때요 asks for an opinion, not a method.

exampleSentence.en: Try taking on a new food.
exampleSentence.note: Use for a challenge, not every tiny attempt.
도와주세요 is the core polite help request.
A practical help request.
Pairs naturally with ㄹ까요 suggestions.
Useful when sequencing a suggestion.
Pairs with 주세요 requests.

exampleSentence.en: May I ask one small favor?
exampleSentence.note: Useful before a request.

exampleSentence.en: Should I try on these clothes?
exampleSentence.note: Core noun for trying on clothing.
Useful in clothing and shopping suggestions.

extendedVocabulary.english: to suit; to look good on

exampleSentence.note: Use the 'to suit' sense, not the 'hang out' sense.

exampleSentence.en: If the size is big, please exchange it.
exampleSentence.note: 바꿔 주세요 is a practical service request.

exampleSentence.ko: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주세요.
exampleSentence.en: Please show me one size smaller too.
exampleSentence.note: 보여 주세요 is the request form used in shops.

extendedDialogue.setting: A shopper tries on clothes, checks the color, and makes polite requests to the staff.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Should I try on these clothes?
lines.grammarNote: 입어 볼까요 asks for an opinion before trying.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 먼저 입어 보세요. 색이 잘 어울려요.
lines.romanization: ne, meonjeo ibeo boseyo. saegi jal eoullyeoyo.
lines.en: Yes, try them on first. The color suits you well.
lines.grammarNote: 입어 보세요 is a soft suggestion.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 이 색도 괜찮은데, 다른 색도 추천해 주세요.
lines.romanization: i saekdo gwaenchaneunde, dareun saekdo chucheon hae juseyo.
lines.en: This color is okay, but please recommend another color too.
lines.grammarNote: 추천해 주세요 is a polite request.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 그럼 이 색도 한번 입어 보세요.
lines.romanization: geureom i saekdo hanbeon ibeo boseyo.
lines.en: Then try on this color too.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 사이즈가 크면 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주세요.
lines.romanization: saijeuga keumyeon han chisu jageun geotdo boyeo juseyo.
lines.en: If the size is big, please show me one size smaller too.
lines.grammarNote: 보여 주세요 is a service request.

readingText.title: Trying before deciding
readingText.body: 민서는 옷 가게에서 재킷을 고르고 있었어요. 직원은 먼저 입어 보세요라고 말했어요. 민서는 이 색도 괜찮지만 다른 색도 보고 싶어서 추천해 달라고 했어요. 직원은 더 밝은 색을 한번 입어 보라고 했고, 민서는 그 색이 더 잘 어울린다고 느꼈어요. 사이즈가 조금 커서 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 달라고 부탁했어요. 이렇게 민서는 바로 결정하지 않고 입어 본 뒤에 선택했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo was choosing a jacket at a clothing store. The staff suggested she try it on first. Minseo asked for another color recommendation, tried a brighter color, and then asked to see one size smaller before deciding.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 직원은 민서에게 먼저 무엇을 해 보라고 했어요?
민서는 왜 추천해 달라고 했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 다른 색도 보고 싶어서 추천해 달라고 했어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 사이즈가 커서 무엇을 부탁했어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 달라고 부탁했어요.

culturalNote.title: Trying sounds softer than deciding
culturalNote.body: In shops, restaurants, and friendly advice, Korean often uses 한번 and -아/어 보다 to lower the pressure. 한번 입어 보세요, 한번 먹어 볼까요, and 한번 가 봐요 all suggest a trial instead of forcing a decision.
culturalNote.tip: When recommending something, combine 한번 with -아/어 보세요: 한번 드셔 보세요, 한번 입어 보세요, 한번 해 보세요.

inlineExercises.prompt: A shopper wants to try on clothes. Which sentence fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -아/어 볼까요 asks about trying an action before deciding.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which is a polite service request?
options: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주세요.
inlineExercises.correct: 한 치수 작은 것도 보여 주세요.
inlineExercises.explanation: -아/어 주세요 turns the action into a polite request.
추천하다 becomes 추천해 주세요 in a polite request.
가다 becomes 갈까요? with ㄹ까요, and 같이 makes the suggestion shared.
Use the 아/어 form before 보다.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다른 색___ 보여 주세요. (Please show me another color.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 보여 주다 takes the thing shown as an object, so 다른 색을 fits. 이 would make the color the subject.
-아/어 보세요 means try doing something. 입다 becomes 입어 보세요.
-(으)ㄹ까요? suggests or asks what to do. 같이 makes the suggestion “together.”

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'Shall we try eating it once?'
inlineExercises.explanation: 한번 softens the idea as “just to try.” 먹어 볼까요? asks whether you should try eating it.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the request: '다른 색 추천해 볼까요?'
inlineExercises.explanation: 추천해 볼까요? asks whether we should try recommending, which is not a service request. 추천해 주세요 asks the other person to recommend something for you.

bullets: V아/어 보다 means try doing: 입어 보세요, 먹어 볼까요, 해 봤어요.
한번 softens trial suggestions: 한번 입어 보세요.
V아/어 주세요 makes polite requests: 추천해 주세요, 보여 주세요, 도와주세요.
Vㄹ/을까요? asks for a shared decision or suggestion: 같이 갈까요?, 주문할까요?

writingTask.prompt: Recommend a restaurant to a friend and gently suggest going together this weekend.
writingTask.hint: Use V-아/어 보다 to nudge them to try it (가 보세요/먹어 보세요), V-아/어 주세요 for a request, and V-(으)ㄹ까요? to suggest going together.
writingTask.model: 이 식당 한번 가 보세요. 정말 맛있어요. 우리 주말에 같이 갈까요? 시간 되면 알려 주세요.
writingTask.modelEn: Try going to this restaurant once. It's really delicious. Shall we go together this weekend? If you have time, please let me know.

canDo: Nudge someone to try something with V-아/어 보다 (한번 먹어 보세요)
Make a polite request with V-아/어 주세요 (알려 주세요)
Float a friendly suggestion with V-(으)ㄹ까요? (같이 갈까요?)
